# 2 Baruch Chapter 8 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 8:1 — "Chaldeans" vs. "Babylonians"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the-Chaldeans" | Literal Syriac kashdaye |
| LOGOS | "the Chaldeans" | Formal, follows biblical designation |
| PNEUMA | "The Babylonians" | "Babylonians" is more recognizable to modern readers |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** LOGOS adopted. "Chaldeans" is the designation used throughout the prophetic corpus (Jer, Ezek, 2 Kgs) and in the Syriac text itself. "Babylonians" is a modernizing substitution that loses the specific ethnic/tribal designation.

---

## 8:3 — "beloved city" vs. "city I loved"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the-beloved-city" | Literal participial adjective |
| LOGOS | "the beloved city" | Formal adjectival phrase |
| PNEUMA | "the city I loved" | Active relative clause; more personal |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** LOGOS adopted. "The beloved city" is the standard expression in Syriac and Hebrew apocalyptic (cf. Rev 21:2). PNEUMA's relative clause unnecessarily shifts from the city as object of devotion to Baruch's personal sentiment.

---

## 8:4 — "ordained" vs. "decreed"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "what-has-been-ordained by-me" | Literal passive with agent |
| LOGOS | "what has been ordained by me" | Formal passive |
| PNEUMA | "what I have decreed" | Active; "decreed" for "ordained" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** LOGOS adopted. "Ordained" preserves the theological sense of divine appointment/determination. "Decreed" shifts the register toward royal/legal rather than theological/apocalyptic.

---

**Total disagreements this chapter: 3**
